query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Small Al additions (e.g., ~2 at%) to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will form a protective alumina-rich surface layer at high temperatures in air, significantly reducing oxygen ingress and improving oxidation resistance relative to the undoped alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy with demonstrated high-temperature mechanical strength but poor oxidation resistance.
generation.intervention: Alloying ~2 at% aluminum into the equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr matrix using standard arc melting or induction melting processes, followed by homogenization heat treatment.
generation.conditions: Evaluated under air atmosphere at 800–1000 °C for up to 5–24 hours, under similar mechanical loading conditions as the baseline alloy was tested (e.g., nominal tensile stress at slow strain rate of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1).
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable external Al2O3 scale at the surface, which impedes inward diffusion of oxygen and prevents accelerated oxidation (“pesting”).
generation.mechanism: The small Al addition leads to selective oxidation of Al at the alloy surface, forming an adherent and impermeable alumina layer that significantly reduces oxygen diffusion and preserves the alloy’s mechanical integrity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the undoped equiatomic alloy, the Al-containing alloy will exhibit measurably lower mass gain, reduced oxide scale thickness, and higher retention of both tensile ductility and high-temperature yield strength after prolonged exposure at 800–1000 °C.
generation.baseline: The unmodified equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has been shown to experience significant oxidation and subsequent mechanical property degradation under similar conditions.
generation.boundary: The protective effect is expected to persist up to ~1000 °C over short-to-intermediate exposures (hours). Severe mechanical or thermal transients or extended exposures at higher temperatures may degrade the alumina scale’s protective efficacy.
generation.uncertainty: The amount of Al required for optimal oxidation resistance while retaining mechanical performance is not yet fully established; excessive Al addition may compromise ductility and toughness.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two batches of HfNbTaTiZr: one equiatomic (control) and one with 2 at% Al added. Apply identical homogenization and sample preparation procedures, then expose samples to air at 900 °C for 24 hours under constant tensile load similar to previous studies.
measurements: Weight gain of each sample after exposure (mass change).
Thickness and morphology of oxide scale (via SEM/EDS).
Residual tensile strength and ductility at room temperature after exposure.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-modified samples do not exhibit a substantial (>50%) reduction in oxide scale thickness or mass gain relative to the baseline, or if their mechanical property retention is not improved, the hypothesis is falsified.
